done.why: The world answered 'BudgetExhausted' while I was stuck inside the Royal Puzzle. I had jammed the ladder block and had no item the steel door's slot would accept.

about: A Zork III style underground adventure. An old man at the bottom of a stair waits for you to prove yourself worthy. You gather things he carries: the amulet, staff, ring, book and key. Along the way you meet a cliff thief, a hooded duellist, a sailor, a freezing lake, a scenic-vista teleporter, a time machine in a museum, and the Royal Puzzle.

ending.what: I went down the secret stair behind the carved wall but was turned back: I was not yet what the old man asked for. I got the amulet, staff and book but never the ring or the key.

moments.note: The cliff thief. I tied the chest to the rope, listened to him count coins, and waited until he hauled me up and gave me the staff.
Saying hello to the sailor was enough to get the vial.
The hooded figure bowed its head and offered its hood. I kept swinging and killed it anyway, which may have been the wrong choice.
I set the time machine to 777 and pressed the button. I died instantly with no warning, and my items were scattered.
I wasted the single-use grue repellent by spraying it underwater, and I had also lost the first application by stopping short of the dark passage.
The scenic vista table cycles through numbered images, and touching it can send you to a deadly altar, a dark room, or a safe room. It is hard to tell which image leads where.
I drank the vial's invisible liquid and nothing happened. I never found out what it was for.
I pushed the ladder block into a position where I could not get out of the Royal Puzzle, and the steel door's slot rejected everything I tried.

wished: A hint about what the slot beside the steel door takes.
A way to reset or leave the Royal Puzzle when stuck.
A warning before the time machine kills you.
To go back and get the ring from the jewel cage and the key.
To find out what the vial liquid was for.

lines.line: Now there's a good friend! Thank you very much, indeed!
lines.why: The thief's mocking politeness made the chest-and-rope trade memorable.

lines.line: The rock has the look of a thing that has been invited many times.
lines.why: A good line that suggests the sword is not just stuck.

lines.line: The water has the look of a cold that would open your hands for you, and would not give back what fell out of them
lines.why: The lake's rule is stated clearly and with style.

lines.line: You go through the door and a few steps down the dark stairs beyond it... The way down is not yours today. You come back up.
lines.why: It tells you the real goal is to gather things elsewhere.

fun.why: The set pieces were fun: the thief, the lake and the time machine. Time was lost to opaque puzzles and to dying and resetting.

engagement.why: There were many places to see and a clear gather-the-items goal. I kept wanting to see everything.

difficulty.why: The lake, the repellent, the table and the puzzle gave little guidance and could not be undone, so a wrong move left me stuck.

interestingness.why: It has many varied locations, lots of texture, and rules that respond to what you do.

prose.why: Rich and witty descriptions with a consistent voice. The expanded text on the lake and the rock stood out.
